# ScreenCue

> ScreenCue is a US$0.99 Windows app that shows your PowerPoint speaker notes in a private, always-on-top teleprompter. Windows leaves the teleprompter out of screen sharing and screen recordings (Windows 10 version 2004 or later, and Windows 11), so your audience sees only your slides. It is made by PeteStudioz.ai and sold on the Microsoft Store, published by Preetam Shenoy.

Key facts:

- Platform: Windows 10 version 1809 or later, and Windows 11. No Mac, mobile or web version.
- Price: US$0.99 one-time purchase on the Microsoft Store (Store ID 9N0VF85M0GS3). No subscription, no in-app purchases.
- Reads speaker notes from .pptx, .pptm, .ppsx, .ppsm and .potx without PowerPoint; .ppt, .pps, .pot and protected or repaired decks through PowerPoint for Windows; also Word (.docx), text (.txt) and Markdown (.md) scripts.
- With "Sync & control PowerPoint" on, it follows the slideshow running in PowerPoint for Windows and can move it forward and back; clickers and arrow keys keep working.
- Privacy: works on the PC; no account, cloud sync, analytics, telemetry or AI service; notes are never uploaded.
- Limits: no automatic scrolling; hiding from capture doesn't apply to a camera pointed at the screen or a hardware capture device; slideshow sync needs PowerPoint desktop for Windows and doesn't work in Windows S mode.
